text.p: Coastal Physician Group Inc. announced on Monday that it has hired Smith Barney Inc. to advise or assist in evaluating on the possible sale of the physician management company.
The decision came after the company, struggling for some time under heavy debt, disclosed last month that it would study ways to maximize shareholder value, including sale of the company.

"We recognize the importance of evaluating all alternatives to enhance Coastal's value for our shareholders, and are continuing to actively explore the sale of the entire company and all other possible strategic or financial transactions ...," President and Chief Executive Joseph Piemont said in a statement released on Monday.
Shares of Coastal ended up 1/2 at 6-3/8.
Coastal provides a broad range of health care and administrative services to physicians, hospitals, employers, managed-care programs and other health care providers.

In the past month alone, a member of its board of directors resigned, and net losses soared to $24.9 million, or $1.04 in the second quarter compared with a loss of $10.5 million, or $0.44, in the same year-ago period.
Coastal attributed the loss for the 1996 second-quarter to contract attrition and lower new business development during the second half of 1995 in the hospital-based contract services division.

It also cited lower net collections per patient visit in the billing and accounts receivable management services division, increased investments associated with the growth in the company's health plans, and increased expenses in information technology.
The company became mired in debt after an aggressive acquisition program that began in July 1993, faltered.

"This resulted in a deterioration of the company's financial performance from net income of $20.7 million, or $0.92 per share, in 1994 to a net loss of $46.9 million, or $1.98 per share, by the end of 1995," the company said in a letter to shareholders printed in the 1995 annual report.
